summary: A 1935 Aermotor fire tower near Hamburg, Arkansas, raised to 120 feet around 1940, decommissioned in 1985, restored 2008-09 and owned by the City of Hamburg.

facts.design: Aermotor steel tower with a 7 by 7 foot observation cab

staffing.status: operated by fire lookout operators 1935 to 1985; decommissioned 1985

events.note: Constructed 1935; NHLR credits the Arkansas Forestry Commission, the handout credits the Aermotor Company design and CCC erection, Wikipedia's infobox gives 1936 but its text says 1935
First listed operator John D. Tucker, 1935 to 1943
20-foot section added, raising the tower to 120 feet; handout and Wikipedia say between 1936 and 1943; NHLR says ca. 1940
Last listed operator Glendine Rauls, 1975 to 1985
Decommissioned in 1985; handout says phased out in favor of aerial fire detection
City of Hamburg purchased the property
Registered with the National Historic Lookout Register June 29, 2005
Added to the National Register of Historic Places March 2, 2006 per Wikipedia
First day of cab restoration May 12, 2008 per NHLR photo caption; handout says the restoration was made possible in 2008
Grand opening for the completed restoration, November 12 and 13, 2009

corrections.why: 30.5 m (100 ft) was the original height; a 20-foot section added between 1936 and 1943 raised the tower to 120 feet.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia's infobox gives 1936, but its text, the NHLR, the handout and Central Lookouts all give 1935. The story uses 1935.
The Register credits the Arkansas Forestry Commission with construction; the handout credits the Aermotor Company design and CCC erection. These can both be true, so the story reports both.
The handout and Wikipedia give a span of 1936 to 1943; the NHLR and Central Lookouts give about 1940. The ranges agree, so the story gives the span and notes the Register's ca. 1940.

notes_for_editor: Current public access is not established by any source read; the story says to check with the City of Hamburg. Living New Deal page returned 403 and was not used. NRHP nomination PDF (Arkansas Preservation) was not reachable. Second search returned no current-status source. The Register credits the Forestry Commission while the handout credits the Aermotor Company and CCC; the story reports both. Wikipedia infobox 1936 conflicts with its text and other sources.
